content:
Other comments has already stated most of the issues. I'd just like to add that this clash is too cryptic for reversed mode imho.

Also: it's quite a shame the author is not fixing those problems; this contribution would make a fine clash for fastest mode and shortest mode.

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: Issues raised haven't been addressed:

* Single-digit input covered in tests only but not in validators.

* The digits 0, 7 and 9 are not covered in tests, and the digit 2 is not covered in validators.

* The range of length of input string is not fully covered (can go up to 100 but actually never exceeds 10).

* The statement is not formatted.

* The stub generator lacks a write statement.

I'll withdraw my rejection once the issues have all been fixed.
There is no test case with a remotely long S despite the constraint saying the length can go up to 100

Goal / Input / Constraints
* Please format "S" as a [[variable]].

Input
* Please format "Line 1" in <<bold>>.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement.

Cases
* Test 4 and Validator 4 aren't aligned. The test covers a single-digit string while the validator covers a multi-digit string. Please revise the validator.

* Please add a new pair of test cases (Test 5 and Validator 5) in which all digits from 0 to 9 are used in randomised order. Both the test and the validator should contain all the digits, but each should use a different ordering.

Thanks.
I feel like there might be a clash like this that already exists. I'm not rejecting this because I could be wrong.
I couldn't find a similar clash, so my main concerns with this contribution are instead the lack of proper statement formatting and insufficient case coverage.
There's also the constraint vs cases mismatch issue as pointed out by @flyon3's comment above.
The idea is quite straightforward, so I'd be surprised if there were no other similar clash. However, duplicate clash of codes aren't as much critical as duplicate classic puzzles, in my opinion.
